catalogue: Australian house-scale electrical, communications and consumer-energy components

objects.name: domestic electrical installation
objects.definition: The fixed supply, metering, switchboards, wiring, protection, earthing, outlets, lighting points and connected fixed equipment forming the electrical installation of a house and its associated structures.
functions: Protect people, wiring and connected equipment
Provide controlled connection points for fixed and portable equipment

cad.pattern: One connected property-wide system branching from supply and switchboards to final points
cad.placement: Across the site, building fabric, service spaces and associated structures
cad.start: Network supply point or independent source
cad.end: Outlets, luminaires, fixed equipment and exposed-conductive-part earthing connections
cad.opening: Requires coordinated entries, penetrations, access and equipment working spaces
cad.load: Electrical equipment and cable loads carried by their enclosures, supports and building substrates

notes: Appliances are included only where they are fixed equipment or materially affect the installed connection; portable consumer products are not decomposed as building members.

objects.name: electricity supply connection assembly
objects.definition: The physical overhead or underground components that connect a property electrical installation to the electricity distributor at the applicable network boundary.
functions: Bring the distributor supply to the property
Provide the service attachment or underground entry
Connect the supply path to consumer mains and service protection

cad.pattern: One selected supply route with distributor-side and customer-side components
cad.placement: Between the street or distribution asset and the main switchboard or meter position
cad.end: Service protection, metering or main switchboard interface
cad.opening: Overhead clearances or underground entry and access are project-specific
cad.load: Cable tension, weight and fault forces transferred through approved supports and enclosures

notes: The ownership boundary and required components vary by distributor and jurisdiction and must be stored as instance metadata.

objects.name: metering and main switchboard assembly
objects.definition: The coordinated enclosure or adjacent enclosures containing the electricity meter, main switches, protective devices, distribution links, earthing terminals, covers and labels at the principal control point of a house installation.
functions: Measure imported and exported electrical energy
Provide main isolation and circuit distribution
House protective, earthing and identification components

cad.pattern: One principal enclosure set with internally ordered service, metering and distribution zones
cad.placement: At the approved accessible meter and main-switchboard position
cad.start: Incoming consumer mains or service protection
cad.opening: Door, escutcheon and device apertures provide controlled access
cad.load: Enclosure and equipment weight fixed to wall, frame, post or cabinet substrate

notes: Meter box and switchboard can share one cabinet or be separate; the selected arrangement must be modelled rather than assumed.

objects.name: final subcircuit distribution system
objects.definition: The protected outgoing circuits, cables, wiring enclosures, junctions and final connection points carrying electricity from a switchboard to lights, socket-outlets and fixed equipment.
functions: Distribute power from protective devices to points of use
Keep circuit conductors together along coordinated routes
Provide switching, isolation and final connections
not_synonyms: one cable without its circuit equipment

cad.pattern: Branching routed circuits from switchboard ways to one or more final points
cad.placement: In wall, floor, ceiling, roof, underground and surface service zones
cad.end: Last outlet, luminaire, isolator or equipment connection
cad.opening: Passes through coordinated holes, sleeves, boxes and fire or air seals
cad.load: Cables and accessories supported independently and by approved building substrates

notes: Circuit rating and cable selection are calculated attributes, not separate geometry classes.

objects.name: domestic earthing and MEN system
objects.definition: The main earthing conductor, earth electrode, protective earthing conductors, earthing terminals, MEN connection and required bonding components that provide the house installation's earthing path.
functions: Connect exposed conductive parts to the earthing system
Provide the main earth reference and fault-current path
Bond selected conductive services and zones where required

cad.pattern: A connected conductor and terminal network radiating from the main earthing terminal to electrode and protected equipment
cad.placement: At the main switchboard, through circuits and at required bonded conductive parts
cad.start: Main earthing terminal and MEN connection
cad.end: Earth electrode, equipment earth terminals and bonding points
cad.opening: Entries and joints remain protected and accessible where required
cad.load: Electrical fault duty; physical loads limited to conductor support and connection forces

notes: MEN means multiple earthed neutral in the Australian supply context; the neutral and protective-earth conductors remain distinct downstream components.

objects.name: overhead electricity service connection
objects.definition: An electricity service arrangement using aerial distributor conductors, a building point of attachment and customer-side conductors or terminals to bring supply to the property.
functions: Transfer conductor tension at the attachment point
Connect the aerial service to consumer mains and service equipment

cad.pattern: One aerial span terminating at a structural attachment and continuing to service equipment
cad.placement: Above ground between network support and building attachment
cad.end: Point of attachment and consumer-side connection
cad.opening: Maintains selected clearances from roofs, openings, ground and other services
cad.load: Conductor tension and wind transferred through service bracket to structure

objects.name: overhead service line
objects.definition: The distributor-side aerial conductor or bundled cable spanning from the electricity network to the property's agreed point of supply or attachment.
functions: Carry distributor supply across the service span
Terminate at the property connection point

cad.pattern: One bundled or grouped aerial run
cad.placement: Between distributor network and property attachment
cad.opening: Clear aerial path
cad.load: Self-weight, wind and tension carried by terminal supports

objects.name: electrical service point of attachment
objects.definition: The nominated building attachment location and hardware where an overhead electricity service is mechanically secured before its electrical connection continues toward the installation.
functions: Transfer service tension to the building structure
Define a coordinated service termination location

cad.pattern: One nominated attachment per overhead service arrangement
cad.placement: On fascia, wall, pole, mast or other approved structural position
cad.opening: Kept clear of prohibited windows, roofs and access zones
cad.load: Service tension transferred through bracket and fixings to verified structure

notes: Point of attachment is a functional location plus physical hardware; point of supply is a network boundary and may not be geometrically identical.

objects.name: overhead electrical service bracket
objects.definition: A metal bracket, hook, eye or mast fitting fixed to structure to carry the mechanical load of an overhead electricity service at its attachment point.
functions: Hold the attachment fitting at the approved position

cad.pattern: One bracket at the service attachment
cad.placement: Fixed into verified fascia, wall, pole, mast or framing
cad.opening: May require a coordinated penetration or backing plate
cad.load: Aerial service tension, wind and self-weight transferred to structure

objects.name: aerial consumer mains
objects.definition: Customer-side insulated mains conductors run above ground from the applicable supply boundary to the main switchboard or metering equipment.
functions: Carry the installation supply on the customer side
Bridge an above-ground route between service and main equipment
Provide active and neutral conductors for the installation supply

cad.pattern: One customer-side aerial mains run
cad.placement: Above ground between service boundary and main switchboard or meter position
cad.opening: Building entry protected and sealed
cad.load: Cable tension and weight carried by approved supports

objects.name: underground electricity service connection
objects.definition: An electricity service arrangement using a buried cable route, conduit or duct and any pit or termination equipment between the distributor network and the property installation.
functions: Bring supply to the property below ground
Connect distributor and consumer-side service equipment

cad.pattern: One buried route with risers and accessible termination points
cad.placement: Below ground between street or network asset and meter or main switchboard
cad.start: Distributor pit, pillar or cable connection
cad.opening: Pit, draw-in and enclosure entries remain accessible and sealed
cad.load: Soil and traffic loads resisted by cover, conduit, cable protection and embedment

objects.name: underground electrical service cable
objects.definition: A power cable selected for the buried or underground service route between the distribution connection and property service equipment.
functions: Resist the selected moisture and mechanical environment
Terminate at network and customer service equipment

cad.pattern: One continuous cable run with documented joints only where selected
cad.placement: In buried conduit, duct or approved direct-buried arrangement
cad.end: Service protection, meter or main switchboard terminals
cad.opening: Cable entries use compatible glands, bushes and seals
cad.load: Pulling, soil and fault forces resisted by cable construction and route protection

objects.name: underground electrical service conduit
objects.definition: A buried conduit or duct providing a protected draw-in pathway for electricity service cables between property connection and service equipment.

cad.pattern: Continuous buried duct with long-radius changes and vertical risers
cad.placement: Between service pit, pillar or boundary and meter or main-switchboard enclosure
cad.opening: Open bore carries cable and draw wire; ends are sealed as selected
cad.load: Soil, traffic and cable-pulling forces resisted by conduit and embedment

objects.name: electrical property connection pit
objects.definition: An accessible underground chamber and cover at or near a property connection that houses distributor cable joints, service terminations or draw-in access where the network arrangement uses a pit.
functions: Protect cable joints and service entries
Join street ducting to the property service route

cad.pattern: One chamber at an underground service junction where used
cad.placement: At verge, boundary or approved property connection location
cad.opening: Removable flush cover provides maintenance access
cad.load: Cover and chamber resist selected pedestrian, landscape or traffic loads

notes: Not every underground service uses a property pit; pillars, cabinets or direct distributor arrangements are alternatives.

objects.name: consumer mains
objects.definition: The customer installation conductors carrying supply from the point of supply to the main switchboard, including an aerial, underground or enclosed route as selected.
functions: Carry the whole-installation supply to the main switchboard
Connect the network boundary to main isolation
Provide active and neutral supply conductors

cad.pattern: One supply run per installation or separately supplied main switchboard
cad.placement: Between point of supply and main switchboard
cad.opening: Entries protected, bushed, glanded and sealed
cad.load: Cable weight, pulling and fault forces carried by supports and terminations

notes: Consumer mains, submains and final subcircuits are different roles even when the cable product looks similar.

objects.name: electrical service protection device
objects.definition: A distributor-approved fuse, circuit breaker or other protective device at the electricity service interface that protects service conductors and associated equipment according to the network arrangement.
functions: Provide a sealed or controlled distributor interface where applicable

cad.pattern: One device or grouped devices at the service interface
cad.placement: Service enclosure, meter panel, pillar or distributor equipment
cad.opening: Controlled cover or seal limits access
cad.load: Electrical fault and terminal forces carried by enclosure and mounting

notes: The generic class does not assume the service protection is a replaceable fuse.

objects.name: electricity service fuse
objects.definition: A replaceable fuse link and carrier used as the service protection device in a network-approved supply arrangement.
functions: Melt and interrupt excessive service current
Fit a controlled service fuse carrier

cad.pattern: One fuse per protected service conductor or network arrangement
cad.placement: Within service fuse carrier or distributor enclosure
cad.opening: Carrier provides controlled removal access
cad.load: Fault current interrupted within rated fuse and carrier

objects.name: electricity meter enclosure
objects.definition: A weather-resistant or indoor cabinet housing electricity meters, meter panels and associated service or switching equipment while providing controlled access for the distributor and occupants.
functions: Control access to live and distributor-sealed sections

cad.pattern: One cabinet or coordinated bank at the approved metering position
cad.placement: Recessed into or surface-mounted on wall, post or service structure
cad.opening: Hinged door and internal panels provide controlled access
cad.load: Cabinet and equipment mass carried by substrate and fixings

notes: A meter box can include a switchboard compartment, but the enclosure and switchboard are not automatically synonymous.

objects.name: electricity meter panel
objects.definition: A rigid insulating or approved mounting panel within a meter enclosure that supports electricity meters, service equipment and their wiring clearances.
functions: Separate equipment from the enclosure backing
Provide arranged cable and terminal access

cad.pattern: One removable or fixed panel carrying arranged meter positions
cad.placement: Inside electricity meter enclosure
cad.opening: Cut-outs and cable access are equipment-specific
cad.load: Meter and service-equipment mass transferred to enclosure

objects.name: electricity meter
objects.definition: A fixed metering device connected at the supply interface to measure electrical energy imported from, and where configured exported to, the electricity network.
functions: Separate metered circuits or tariffs where configured

cad.pattern: One or more meters arranged on the meter panel
cad.placement: Within approved meter enclosure or metering cabinet
cad.opening: Display and authorised access remain visible or reachable
cad.load: Device mass and terminal forces carried by meter panel

notes: Whether the meter is distributor-owned and its exact wiring arrangement are jurisdictional instance data.

objects.name: smart electricity meter
objects.definition: An electronic electricity meter that records interval energy data and includes communications equipment for remote reading, service functions or tariff operation.
functions: Measure import and export energy in time intervals
Support remote or configured metering functions

cad.pattern: One or more smart meters on the meter panel
cad.placement: Approved meter enclosure with communications access
cad.opening: Display, seals and communications clearances remain available
cad.load: Meter mass and terminal forces carried by panel

notes: Smart describes metering and communication capability, not a different enclosure shape.

objects.name: main switchboard
objects.definition: The principal switchboard containing the installation main switch or switches and distributing supply to submains and final subcircuits through protective and control devices.
functions: House protection, earthing, neutral and identification components

cad.pattern: One principal board with ordered incoming, main-switch and outgoing-device zones
cad.placement: At the main switchboard position, within or beside metering equipment
cad.start: Incoming consumer mains or metered supply
cad.opening: Door and escutcheon expose only intended controls during ordinary operation
cad.load: Enclosure and device mass supported by cabinet, wall or mounting frame

objects.name: switchboard enclosure
objects.definition: A metal or insulating cabinet that contains and protects switchboard devices, busbars, links and wiring while providing mounting surfaces and controlled access.
functions: Provide cable entries, covers and environmental protection

cad.pattern: One cabinet around each distribution-board assembly
cad.placement: Surface-mounted or recessed at accessible board location
cad.opening: Door, device apertures and cable knockouts are controlled openings
cad.load: Devices and cables supported through enclosure to substrate

objects.name: switchboard enclosure door
objects.definition: A hinged or removable outer cover closing a switchboard enclosure while allowing ordinary access to labelled device controls and the internal escutcheon.
functions: Protect device controls from environment and accidental contact
Carry labels, locks or viewing features where selected

cad.pattern: One door per enclosure compartment where fitted
cad.placement: Front face of switchboard enclosure
cad.opening: Requires unobstructed swing and access zone
cad.load: Door self-weight carried by hinges

objects.name: switchboard escutcheon
objects.definition: An internal protective panel with device apertures that screens live switchboard parts while leaving approved switch handles and indicators accessible.
functions: Prevent ordinary contact with live parts
Separate the wiring space from user-operable controls

cad.pattern: One fitted panel over each accessible device row or board interior
cad.placement: Behind outer door and in front of switchgear
cad.opening: Only documented device apertures and fixing access
cad.load: Self-weight and access loads carried by enclosure fixings

objects.name: switchboard DIN rail
objects.definition: A standardised metal mounting rail fixed inside an enclosure to support clip-on circuit breakers, RCBOs, switches and other modular electrical devices.
functions: Provide a common modular mounting profile
Transfer device loads to the enclosure

cad.pattern: Parallel rail rows sized to modular device ways
cad.placement: Inside switchboard enclosure behind escutcheon
cad.opening: Device clips engage the rail profile
cad.load: Device weight and operating forces transferred to enclosure

objects.name: electrical installation main switch
objects.definition: A switch or circuit-breaker device in the main switchboard identified to isolate the whole installation supply or a defined source such as grid, solar or battery supply.
functions: Connect or disconnect a complete supply source
Present an accessible operating handle and status

cad.pattern: One identified main switch per supply source or required isolated section
cad.placement: Prominent position within main switchboard
cad.opening: Handle projects through escutcheon aperture
cad.load: Switching and fault forces contained by device and rail mounting

notes: Main switch is a role. A circuit breaker may perform it, but not every circuit breaker is a main switch.

objects.name: miniature circuit breaker
objects.definition: A resettable modular protective device that opens a circuit when current exceeds its overcurrent or short-circuit operating characteristics.
functions: Interrupt short-circuit current within its rating
Provide manual circuit switching and reset

cad.pattern: Repeated modular devices aligned on DIN rail
cad.placement: Switchboard row behind escutcheon
cad.opening: Operating toggle and marking visible through escutcheon
cad.load: Fault energy contained by rated device and board assembly

notes: An MCB provides overcurrent protection but not residual-current protection unless combined in an RCBO.

objects.name: residual current circuit-breaker
objects.definition: A residual-current protective switching device without integral overcurrent protection, used with separate overcurrent protection for the circuit or group it protects.
functions: Disconnect supply when residual current reaches its operating condition
Provide a test control and manual switching

cad.pattern: One device protecting one or a documented group of circuits
cad.placement: Switchboard DIN rail beside associated overcurrent devices
cad.opening: Toggle and test button visible through escutcheon
cad.load: Switching and fault forces contained by device and board

notes: RCD is the broad protective-function family; RCCB names the device without integral overcurrent protection.

objects.name: residual current circuit-breaker with overcurrent protection
objects.definition: A modular protective device combining residual-current protection and circuit-breaker overcurrent protection for one circuit in a single unit.
functions: Provide manual isolation, test and reset at the switchboard

possible_aliases.term: combined safety switch and circuit breaker

cad.pattern: One modular device per protected final subcircuit where selected
cad.placement: Switchboard DIN rail behind escutcheon
cad.end: Protected active and neutral circuit conductors
cad.opening: Toggle and test button visible through escutcheon
cad.load: Fault and switching energy contained by rated device and board

objects.name: electrical cartridge fuse
objects.definition: A replaceable cylindrical or blade-ended fuse link containing a calibrated element that melts to interrupt overcurrent when installed in its compatible holder.

cad.pattern: One replaceable fuse per protected pole or equipment input
cad.placement: Inside compatible fuse carrier or isolator-fuse
cad.opening: Removed only through the holder access method
cad.load: Fault energy interrupted within fuse rating

objects.name: electrical fuse carrier
objects.definition: An insulating holder with contacts, terminals and a removable carrier or cover that houses a compatible fuse and connects it into a circuit.
functions: Hold and electrically connect the fuse
Allow controlled fuse replacement or isolation

cad.pattern: One carrier per fused pole or grouped device
cad.placement: Switchboard rail, panel or equipment enclosure
cad.opening: Carrier opens or withdraws for fuse access
cad.load: Fuse fault energy and operating forces contained by holder

objects.name: surge protection device
objects.definition: A device connected between live conductors and the earthing system to limit transient overvoltage by diverting surge current through a controlled protective path.
functions: Indicate protection status or end of life where provided

cad.pattern: One device or coordinated pole set near the protected board supply
cad.placement: Switchboard DIN rail with short connections to live conductors and earth
cad.opening: Status window and replaceable module remain accessible
cad.load: Surge current and thermal duty contained by selected device and conductors

objects.name: switchboard busbar
objects.definition: A rigid conductive bar within a switchboard that distributes current between an incoming connection and multiple devices or outgoing circuits.
functions: Reduce loose inter-device wiring where the board design uses a busbar

cad.pattern: One or more parallel bars or modular distribution strips
cad.placement: Inside switchboard enclosure behind escutcheon
cad.start: Incoming main switch or supply terminal
cad.opening: Protected by shrouds and board covers
cad.load: Current and fault forces resisted by conductor section and insulated supports

objects.name: modular comb busbar
objects.definition: An insulated distribution bar with repeated teeth or pins spaced to feed a row of compatible modular switchboard devices.

cad.pattern: One repeated-tooth strip across a compatible device row
cad.placement: At supply terminals of adjacent DIN devices
cad.end: Last supplied device and insulated end
cad.opening: Teeth enter device terminals; unused ends remain protected
cad.load: Current and fault forces resisted by busbar and device terminals

objects.name: switchboard active link
objects.definition: An insulated terminal block or bar joining one incoming active conductor to multiple outgoing active conductors within a switchboard arrangement.
functions: Organise conductor branching within the board

cad.pattern: One link per active distribution group where used
cad.placement: Inside switchboard enclosure on insulated mounting
cad.opening: Covered terminal entries
cad.load: Current and terminal clamping forces carried by link and support

objects.name: switchboard neutral link
objects.definition: An insulated terminal bar within a switchboard that joins the incoming neutral to outgoing neutral conductors while keeping their circuit terminations organised and accessible for testing.
functions: Connect to the MEN link at the main switchboard arrangement

cad.pattern: One or more links grouped by neutral or residual-current protection arrangement
cad.placement: Inside switchboard on insulated support
cad.end: Outgoing circuit neutrals and MEN connection where applicable
cad.opening: Individual terminal entries remain accessible for authorised work
cad.load: Neutral current and terminal forces carried by bar and support

notes: A neutral link is insulated from the enclosure; it is not the same physical or electrical role as the earth bar.

objects.name: switchboard earth bar
objects.definition: A conductive terminal bar bonded to the switchboard earthing arrangement for terminating protective earthing conductors, the main earthing conductor and selected bonding conductors.
functions: Provide the main earthing terminal function where arranged
Connect earthing and bonding paths within the board

cad.pattern: One bar or coordinated bars with repeated conductor terminals
cad.placement: Inside main or distribution switchboard
cad.start: Main earthing conductor and MEN link
cad.opening: Terminals accessible only within authorised board access
cad.load: Fault current and clamping forces carried by bar, bonds and enclosure

objects.name: switchboard pole filler
objects.definition: A small insulating blank fitted into an unused modular-device opening in a switchboard escutcheon to close the gap and preserve protection from contact with internal parts.
functions: Allow future device positions without replacing the whole escutcheon

cad.pattern: Repeated blanks filling every unused device aperture
cad.placement: Escutcheon openings without installed modular devices
cad.opening: Closes rather than creates the opening
cad.load: Retained by clips against incidental contact

objects.name: switchboard circuit schedule
objects.definition: A fixed printed, engraved or handwritten schedule at a switchboard that maps each protective or switching device to the circuit, area or equipment it controls.
functions: Support safe isolation and fault finding
Record spare ways and source designations
not_synonyms: circuit identification label on one device

cad.pattern: One schedule per switchboard
cad.placement: Inside door, beside devices or at another durable visible board location
cad.opening: Does not obstruct vents, controls or access
cad.load: Negligible label load

notes: Schedule content is instance metadata, but the durable schedule itself is a physical identification object.

objects.name: electrical circuit identification label
objects.definition: A durable label fixed beside a switch, breaker, isolator, outlet or cable to identify its circuit, source, controlled equipment or function.
functions: Distinguish normal, alternative and generated supplies

cad.pattern: Repeated labels at every selected identification point
cad.placement: Adjacent to or on the identified device, cable or enclosure
cad.opening: Must not obstruct controls, vents or terminals
cad.load: Negligible label load

objects.name: electrical warning label
objects.definition: A durable sign or label fixed to electrical equipment to warn of a specific electrical hazard, multiple supply, generated supply, battery, solar DC or other documented condition.
functions: Warn users and workers of electrical hazards
Identify unusual or multiple supply conditions
Direct attention before opening, isolating or working

cad.pattern: One or more labels at each documented warning location
cad.placement: Switchboards, isolators, equipment, enclosures and supply points
cad.opening: Does not obscure controls or access
cad.load: Negligible label load

notes: The existence of a label object does not authorise invented wording; text must come from the applicable current path.

objects.name: electrical distribution sub-board
objects.definition: A downstream distribution board supplied by a submain and containing isolation, protective devices, links, earthing terminals and outgoing circuits for a defined building area or outbuilding.
functions: Distribute supply near a group of loads
Provide local circuit protection and isolation
Reduce long final-circuit routing from the main switchboard

cad.pattern: One downstream board per selected load group or separate structure
cad.placement: Accessible location near served circuits
cad.opening: Door and escutcheon provide controlled access
cad.load: Board and equipment weight transferred to wall, cabinet or post

notes: An outbuilding sub-board earthing arrangement must be modelled from the selected design; do not add a second MEN link by default.

objects.name: electrical submain
objects.definition: A set of conductors carrying supply from one switchboard to another switchboard or distribution point rather than directly to a final point of use.
functions: Supply a downstream board or distribution point
Carry active, neutral and earthing conductors as designed
Connect upstream protection to downstream isolation and distribution

cad.pattern: One routed supply run between boards
cad.placement: In building cavities, conduit, tray, underground or overhead as selected
cad.opening: Entries use compatible glands, bushes, seals and firestopping
cad.load: Cable weight, pulling and fault forces carried by supports and terminations

objects.name: metering isolation device
objects.definition: A switch or isolating device installed in a metering arrangement to disconnect supply to specified metering or downstream equipment where the distributor-approved design provides one.
functions: Provide controlled isolation for metering work
Present an identified operating and sealing arrangement

cad.pattern: One device where required by the selected metering arrangement
cad.placement: Metering or service compartment
cad.opening: Handle or seal access remains controlled
cad.load: Switching and fault forces contained by device and enclosure

notes: This is optional geometry: not every jurisdiction or metering arrangement uses a separate meter isolator.

objects.name: MEN link
objects.definition: A removable or fixed conductor or link at the main switchboard that connects the installation neutral to the main earthing terminal in the multiple earthed neutral arrangement.
functions: Connect neutral and earthing systems at the designated point
Support the intended earth-fault current path

cad.pattern: One designated connection at the main switchboard arrangement
cad.placement: Between neutral link and main earthing terminal or earth bar
cad.end: Main earthing terminal or earth bar
cad.opening: Accessible only within authorised switchboard access
cad.load: Earth-fault current and terminal forces carried by link

notes: Do not automatically repeat the MEN link at a sub-board or outbuilding; use the documented earthing arrangement.

objects.name: main earthing conductor
objects.definition: The conductor connecting the main earthing terminal or earth bar of an electrical installation to its earth electrode.
functions: Connect the main earthing terminal to earth electrode
Form the principal electrode connection of the earthing system

cad.pattern: One direct continuous route between main earthing terminal and electrode
cad.placement: From main switchboard earthing bar to ground electrode
cad.opening: Passes through protected entries and remains identifiable
cad.load: Fault current carried electrically; conductor physically supported along route

objects.name: electrical earth electrode
objects.definition: A conductive rod, strip, plate or other approved electrode installed in contact with the ground and connected to the main earthing conductor.
functions: Receive the main earthing conductor through an accessible clamp

cad.pattern: One or more documented electrodes forming the installation electrode arrangement
cad.placement: In ground near the installation with protected accessible connection
cad.start: Accessible conductor clamp near ground surface
cad.opening: Clamp may sit within inspection enclosure
cad.load: Ground insertion and corrosion exposure; negligible building load

notes: Electrode form and number are project inputs; the ontology does not assume one universal driven rod.

objects.name: earth electrode clamp
objects.definition: A corrosion-resistant mechanical connector securing the main earthing conductor to the earth electrode while keeping the electrical joint inspectable where required.
functions: Allow inspection or testing of the electrode connection

cad.pattern: One clamp at each main conductor-to-electrode connection
cad.placement: At accessible top or connection point of earth electrode
cad.opening: Inspection enclosure provides access where installed
cad.load: Conductor clamping force and environmental exposure

objects.name: earth electrode inspection enclosure
objects.definition: A small ground-level pit, box or cover protecting the top of an earth electrode and its clamp while permitting inspection and test access.
functions: Mark the electrode location at ground level

cad.pattern: One enclosure around each electrode connection requiring ground-level access
cad.placement: Flush with or just above finished ground at earth electrode
cad.opening: Cover opens to expose clamp and conductor
cad.load: Cover resists selected foot, landscape or light traffic loads

objects.name: protective earthing conductor
objects.definition: A conductor connecting exposed conductive equipment parts and circuit earth terminals back to the switchboard earthing terminal so protective devices can operate under an earth fault.
functions: Connect equipment earth terminals to the earthing system
Maintain protective continuity along a circuit or submain

cad.pattern: One continuous protective path following each applicable circuit or submain
cad.placement: Within cable, wiring enclosure or dedicated bonded route
cad.opening: Passes through the same coordinated entries as circuit conductors
cad.load: Fault current carried electrically; conductor supported with the circuit

objects.name: electrical earthing terminal
objects.definition: A screw, clamp, stud or terminal provided on electrical equipment or an accessory for connecting a protective earthing or bonding conductor.
functions: Bond a conductive enclosure or equipment part
materials: copper alloy or plated steel terminal

cad.pattern: One or more terminals at each equipment earthing point
cad.placement: On equipment frame, enclosure, accessory or terminal block
cad.opening: Terminal access remains available for authorised connection
cad.load: Conductor clamping and fault-current duty

objects.name: equipotential bonding conductor
objects.definition: A conductor joining selected conductive parts or services to the earthing system so their accessible electrical potential is controlled together in the documented installation arrangement.
functions: Connect a bonding point to the earthing terminal or bonded network

cad.pattern: Dedicated conductors linking each selected bonding point
cad.placement: Between conductive service, pool zone, structural part or equipment and earthing system
cad.start: Bonding clamp or terminal on conductive part
cad.end: Earth bar or documented bonding node
cad.opening: Protected entries and accessible connection points
cad.load: Bonding and fault current carried electrically; conductor physically supported

objects.name: electrical bonding clamp
objects.definition: A purpose-made clamp fixed around a conductive pipe, bar or other approved part to connect an equipotential bonding conductor without relying on incidental contact.
functions: Clamp to the selected conductive part

cad.pattern: One clamp at each selected bonded conductive part without an integral terminal
cad.placement: Around pipe, bar or approved conductive element at accessible location
cad.opening: Clamp encircles or grips host without obstructing service access
cad.load: Clamping force and fault-current duty

objects.name: pool equipotential bonding assembly
objects.definition: The conductors, clamps, lugs and accessible bonding points connecting selected conductive pool reinforcement, shells, fittings, equipment and nearby conductive parts into the documented equipotential bonding arrangement.
functions: Connect the pool bonding network to the electrical earthing system
not_synonyms: protective earth to one pump alone

cad.pattern: A bonding network around and through selected conductive pool components
cad.placement: Within pool shell, plant area and documented surrounding zones
cad.start: Bonded pool reinforcement, fittings and equipment
cad.opening: Test and connection points remain accessible where required
cad.load: Bonding current duty; conductors protected from concrete placement, corrosion and damage

notes: The ontology identifies physical bonding parts but does not invent universal pool-zone distances or connection details.

objects.name: conductive service bonding connection
objects.definition: A bonding conductor, clamp or terminal arrangement connecting a selected conductive building service such as metallic water pipework to the electrical earthing system where required by the installation design.
functions: Maintain an accessible route to the earthing system
not_synonyms: using a water pipe as an earth electrode

cad.pattern: One connection at each selected conductive service bonding point
cad.placement: Accessible point on metallic service near the documented entry or equipment location
cad.opening: Connection remains accessible and does not obstruct service valves or joints
cad.load: Bonding current and clamping forces

notes: Plastic pipework is not made conductive by naming it a service bond; actual material and continuity must be known.

objects.name: electrical final subcircuit
objects.definition: A protected circuit extending from a switchboard protective device to one or more final outlets, lights, isolators or fixed-equipment connection points without supplying another switchboard.
functions: Carry electricity to final points of use
Coordinate active, neutral and protective earthing conductors
